_: THE COMMITTED AST CORPUS. Hand-written, one case per row, each with the reason it exists. A corpus generated from the thing it measures is not an oracle, so nothing here was produced by a parser or an interpreter.
_shape: `ast` is the CANONICAL PERSISTED tree (Task 3's `canonicalise` output), not jsep's: five node types `num` / `series` / `op` / `call` / `offset`, and the union of keys over any tree is exactly ['args','name','type','value'] -- `offset` carries {type,value,args} and deliberately NO `name`, so the key vocabulary is unmoved. `source` rides alongside for editing and read-back and is NEVER the input to anything that computes; Task 3 owes the rail asserting canonicalise(parse(source)) deep-equals `ast` for every row here.
_coverage: Every entry of `app/src/components/chart/engine/ast/closedTable.json` must appear in at least one case. That floor is DERIVED FROM THE MANIFEST by `tools/ast_conformance.py::assert_corpus_covers_the_table`, never hand-listed here -- DPC's four constants rode outside their rail for the rule's entire life because that rail was a LIST of what somebody remembered. The manifest does not exist until Task 3, so the rail is ARMED AND SKIPPED and Task 3 owes its first pass.
_operators: The canonical tree names unary minus `u-` and the ternary `?:`, matching the manifest's operator keys. The SOURCE spells them `-` and `? :`; that difference is the canonicaliser's job and is exactly what Task 3's round-trip rail pins.

cases.why: the simplest reduction; covers `sma` and the `close` series identifier
the 200-warmup half is NaN for 199 bars and the SUBTRACTION must stay NaN, never 0
JS `/` and Python `/` are both float. `//` is in NEITHER table and this pins that it cannot arrive by accident
a comparison against NaN is false in both languages -- the one place they agree by luck, so it is pinned rather than assumed
the only branching form in the table
composition depth: the lanes must agree on evaluation ORDER, not only on each node
the {0,1,NaN} event shape spec 3.1 requires, produced by a formula rather than a native

`crossUnder` is a SEPARATE table entry, not `!crossOver` -- both are {0,1,NaN} and both are false on the bar a series merely stays below, so a lane that derived one from the other would disagree on the very first bar

`volume` is the one series whose magnitude is six orders off the price series, so a relative-tolerance comparison that silently used an ABSOLUTE epsilon would pass on price and fail here -- and it is the only case that reads the `v` field
`lowest` is not `-highest(-x)`; it is its own table entry with its own warmup, and this is the only case that reads the `l` field as a whole-window reduction

covers `+`, `*` and `stdev` in one expression whose PRECEDENCE is the point: a canonical tree that bound `+` tighter than `*` would still evaluate, still be finite, and be wrong by a band width. `stdev` is also the one entry where a population/sample divisor disagreement between the lanes is invisible in the shape and visible only in the number

`change` is the only lookback-1 entry, so it is the only place a lane can disagree about what bar 0 is (NaN, or 0 because there is no previous bar). `abs` composed on top proves the disagreement is not laundered into a magnitude

`min`/`max` are ELEMENTWISE over two series, not reductions over one, and their NaN rule is the opposite of a comparison's: JS `Math.max(NaN, x)` is NaN while Python's `max` returns whichever it meets first. That is a real divergence and it can only be caught by pinning it

the strict `<` against a running minimum is FALSE on every bar of a correct implementation and TRUE on any bar of an off-by-one one, so it is the cheapest possible detector of a window boundary that shifted by a bar

covers `>=`, `<=` and `&&`. The INCLUSIVE comparisons are the ones a `>`/`>=` slip hides in: C Task 3's M5 survived both committed oracles because an indicator landing exactly on a threshold is measure-zero on real tape -- here `close <= high` is true AT EQUALITY on every bar whose close IS the high, which this series contains

covers `==`, `!=`, `!` and `||`. Float equality on real tape is the one operator whose result is decided by the LAST BIT, so the two lanes either read the same double or they do not; and `!`/`||` pin that a boolean column is {0,1,NaN} in both lanes rather than JS's `false`/Python's `False`

the canonical tree names unary minus `u-` while the source spells it `-`, so this is the one case whose AST cannot be read off its source by eye. It is deliberately the shape Task 3's round-trip rail is most likely to catch a canonicaliser getting wrong

THE ACCEPTANCE EXPRESSION. Phase F exists because a member could not write it: eleven functions and not one of them an indicator. It covers `rsi`, and because it is a COMPARISON its column is 0/1 at every bar -- so the digest also pins that an indicator composes into a CONDITION rather than only into a line.

⭐ THE FINITE-TAIL CONTRACT, AND IT IS THE ONE CASE NO GOLDEN INDICATOR FIXTURE CAN CARRY. `indicators.js` and `indicator_compute.py` are written for BARS and a bar is finite; hand `compute_atr_raw` a NaN and Python's `max` keeps the incumbent while `Math.max` returns NaN -- a real cross-lane divergence no fixture contains, because no fixture contains a NaN. Both walkers therefore start the shipped maths after the last non-finite input value. The first value here lands at bar 33, exactly the 19 + 14 the manifest's tree sum promises; a poisoned Wilder seed would make the whole column NaN, which this digest would show as every row null.
the MACD LINE, and the first three-argument call in the table. Its lookback is `arg2`, so this also pins that `maxLookback` reads the argument the declaration NAMES rather than the last one.

⭐ THE MANIFEST MAKES A CLAIM HERE AND THIS ROW PAYS FOR IT. `_functions_excluded.macdSignal` says the signal line is not declarable -- its window is `slow + signal`, a sum of two arguments -- but IS expressible as this composition. Measured against `compute_macd_raw(...)[1]` the two agree at 0.0 relative error, so the exclusion costs a member a longer spelling and nothing else. If `ema`'s NaN-restart or `macd`'s alignment ever moved, this digest moves and the claim stops being true LOUDLY.
Wilder's average true range over the three series it is defined on -- the first four-argument call, and the first case whose bars are packed from three separate declared columns rather than one.

the +DI leg of the directional movement index. `adx` itself is refused (`_functions_excluded.adx` -- its window is `2 * period`, which no single declaration can say), so this and `minus_di` are what keep the DI cross expressible and that refusal honest.

the -DI leg. Separate from `plus_di` on purpose: both come out of ONE call to the shipped `computeADX` / `compute_adx_raw`, so a binding that read the wrong tuple slot would agree with itself and only two digests can see it.
fast %K. The shipped implementation returns %K and %D from one call; this entry declares only %K, and `d_period` is pinned to 1 so it cannot reach a guard the declaration says nothing about.

⭐ THE SECOND CLAIM THE MANIFEST MAKES, AND THIS ROW PAYS FOR IT. `_functions_excluded.stochD` says %D is not declarable (window `kPeriod + dPeriod`) but IS the simple mean of %K -- which is literally how `compute_stoch_raw` computes it. Measured against that column the two agree at 3.2e-16 relative, inside 1e-9 with seven orders of margin, so the exclusion is a spelling cost and not a capability gap.

the commodity channel index -- the one bound indicator whose maths runs on the TYPICAL price `(h + l + c) / 3` rather than on a single column, so it is the case that would notice a binding packing the three columns in the wrong order.

Williams %R. ⚠️ THE NAME IS `williamsR` HERE AND `williams_r` IN `indicator_compute._CASE_COLUMNS` -- the two-vocabularies split the closed table's own header opens with. This row is where the two are made to answer for one number.

the money flow index, and the only bound indicator that reads VOLUME -- so it is the one case that would catch a binding whose bar packing dropped or misnamed the `v` field. Five arguments, the widest call the table declares apart from the Ichimoku lagging span.
the top of the Donchian channel. All three Donchian lines come out of ONE shipped call, so each earns its own digest for the same reason the two DI legs do.

the Donchian midline -- `(highest high + lowest low) / 2`, which is also the formula every Ichimoku midline uses. Declared because a member reaching for a turtle breakout should not have to know it is the mean of two extremes.
the bottom of the Donchian channel.

the conversion line. ⚠️ ALL THREE PERIODS ARE ARGUMENTS EVEN THOUGH THIS LINE USES ONE, because the shipped implementation starts EVERY line at `senkouB - 1`. Declaring `lookback: arg4` is therefore the truth about this column's warm-up; a two-argument `tenkan(high, low, 9)` would have declared a 9-bar window over a column that is NaN for 51 bars.
the base line. `close > ichimokuKijun(high, low, 9, 26, 52)` is the ordinary Ichimoku trend filter, and the tenkan/kijun cross is `crossOver` of this and the row above.

leading span A. ⚠️ NOT FORWARD-DISPLACED, and that is inherited rather than chosen: `indicators.js` records the deviation deliberately (the cloud sits over the price that produced it) and `compute_ichimoku_raw` mirrors it. So this column's forward reach really is 0 and the badge says `non-repainting` truthfully.
leading span B -- the 52-bar midline, and the line whose own period IS the family's declared lookback.

⭐⭐ THE FORWARD REFERENCE, AND THE ONLY ONE IN THE TABLE. `chikou[j]` IS `close[j + 26]` -- the exact construction `closedTable.json::_no_offset` names as the thing the repaint linter has to be able to decide. It is the first and only entry declaring a `forward`, so it is the first tree in the product that lints `preview-repaints` rather than `non-repainting`. ⚠️ ITS PAD IS AT THE END, not the start: the last 26 slots are NaN because those bars' lagging value has not happened yet, and this digest is what would notice a binding that quietly shifted the column the other way.

the single most-used construct in Pine and TC2000 (`close[1]` / `C1`), and the smallest thing that can carry the LEFT-EDGE rule: bar 0 has no prior bar, so the answer is NOT COMPUTABLE -- never 0.0 and never the first bar's close

`x[0]` is `x`, and the parse door FOLDS it rather than emitting a zero-bar node -- one column must have ONE canonical tree, because `astHash` decides whether an edit bumps `compute.rev` and a rev bump force-migrates every binding. Here so the fold is pinned by the round-trip rail rather than left as a comment

the idiom the whole Pine corpus is full of. The subtraction must stay NOT COMPUTABLE on bar 0 rather than collapsing to 0.0 -- a fabricated zero here is a bar-over-bar change a user can arm an alert on

⭐ THE NESTING CASE THE TREE SUM EXISTS FOR: maxLookback is 22, not 20 and not 2. The offset shifts the ARGUMENT, so the warmup prefix is the sum of both windows and the two lanes must pad the same 21 bars

the other nesting order, and it is NOT the same column: shifting the RESULT of a 20-bar mean reads the mean of bars [i-21, i-2]. Same maxLookback of 22, different values -- so a lane that composed the two orders together would agree on the budget and disagree on the numbers

an offset over a 0/1 column. NaN must PROPAGATE through the pad rather than the comparison's own `NaN -> 0` rule reaching it: the bar before bar 0 did not happen, which is not the same fact as `close was not above open`
two different offsets under one operator: the comparison is not computable until BOTH sides are, so the pad is the deeper of the two (3), not the shallower and not their sum

the simplest recurrence, and the one whose ANSWER proves the design: a counter re-seeded every 12 bars reads 12 on every bar it answers and nothing on the eleven before. A single forward pass from the first fetched bar would read 1, 2, 3 ... here instead, and that number changes the moment the chart is panned -- which is the whole reason the window re-seeds

a pointwise call in the recurrence spine, and an INDEPENDENT check on the maths: this is `highest(close, 20)` written as a recurrence, so both lanes are pinned against a shipped function rather than against a number somebody typed. The scalar `max` the step loop applies is the same object `FN.max` lifts, which is why their NaN rule cannot drift apart

the ternary in the spine, which is how a state machine is spelled: the flag latches on an up bar and CARRIES until the window re-seeds. It forgets its seed the first time the condition fires, so a naive one-pass implementation would agree with this on most bars and disagree on the rest -- the hardest kind of wrong to see

the PARTITION, in one case. `sma(close, 10)` reads no running value, so it is evaluated ONCE as a column and indexed per step; both lanes must put it on the same side of that split. And the lookback composes rather than replacing: this tree reaches 30 bars back, not 20

an offset OF a recurrence, which is legal, as against the binding UNDER an offset, which is refused by `interpret:recurrence`. That distinction is the boundary itself: a finished column has a history and can be shifted, while the step loop holds one previous value and has none. The pad is 9 -- the offset plus the warm-up

Wilder's smoothing, which is `ta.rma` and the average inside every RSI and ATR ever written. It shares ONE implementation with `ema` and differs only in the alpha (1/n against 2/(n+1)), so this case pins that the SEED and the restart-on-a-hole did not fork when the second constant arrived -- the identity `rma(x, n) == ema(x, 2n-1)` holds for the recurrence and NOT for the seed, which is the trap

the linearly weighted average: the newest bar carries weight n and the oldest carries 1. Both lanes must divide by the same n(n+1)/2 and must let a NaN in the window POISON the result rather than quietly averaging the bars that happened to be there

⛔ THE ONE CASE IN THIS CORPUS THAT EXISTS BECAUSE THE TWO LANGUAGES DISAGREE BY DEFAULT. JS rounds a half toward +inf, Python rounds it to even, Pine rounds it away from zero -- three answers for `-2.5`. Scaling a price difference by 100 is what puts real halves in the input, so this is not a synthetic probe

-1, 0 or 1, and the zero is the point: `Math.sign(-0)` is -0 in JS and `copysign(1, -0.0)` is -1.0 in Python, so both lanes write the three answers out. Composed over `change` so the first bar is a genuine hole rather than a fabricated zero

⭐ ONE OF THE TWO ENTRIES THAT DO NOT PROPAGATE NaN -- it INSPECTS it. Over a 20-bar average the answer is 1 for the whole warm-up and 0 after, which makes this the only case in the corpus whose value is DEFINED on bars every other case reports as not computable

the other one, and the dangerous one: it turns not-computable into a value the user named. `_functions_na` argues for declaring it at length; this case pins that both lanes replace on exactly the same bars and neither invents a default. The replacement is `close` rather than 0 so that a lane silently substituting zero is visible in the numbers rather than only at the edges
the square root of a positive series -- the happy path beside the negative-root case
a NEGATIVE root on every bar -- JS says NaN, Python raises; both must say NaN
the natural log of a positive series -- the happy path beside the ln(0) case
ln(0) on every bar -- JS says -Infinity, Python raises; both must say NaN
the base-10 log, which TC2000 spells CLG while spelling the natural one LOG
exp(0) is 1 on every bar -- the ordinary case beside the overflow one
drives exp past the largest representable exponent; both lanes must answer NaN, never Infinity
close squared -- the tree the `^` operator rewrites to, and the ordinary pow case
a negative base with a fractional exponent: Python returns a COMPLEX number, JS returns NaN
a NEGATIVE left operand -- Python's % is floored and TC2000 truncates, so the sign must follow the left
a zero divisor on every bar -- neither lane may raise, and neither may answer an infinity
integer division truncating toward zero on a negative
the sine over an unbounded input; the ordinary trig case both lanes must agree on
the cosine over an unbounded input; the ordinary trig case both lanes must agree on
the tangent, which grows large near pi/2 but is never actually infinite in floating point
the arctangent, which TC2000 spells ARCTAN; bounded output over an unbounded input
sinh(0) is 0 -- the ordinary case
drives sinh past the representable range; both lanes must answer NaN
a rolling sum -- the reduction TradingView scripts reach for most after the averages
Pine's ta.dev, the MEAN ABSOLUTE deviation -- CCI is defined on this, not on stdev
the two deviations differ on every real series; this column is the proof and must not be zero

⛔ ADX ENTERED THE TABLE 2026-08-11 WITH NO CROSS-LANE CASE, so its JS<->Python agreement was asserted by nobody -- `assert_corpus_covers_the_table` went red naming it and that red is what surfaced this. It is the only declared function whose `lookback` is `2*arg3` rather than a bare `argN`, so this case is also the one place the multiplied-window grammar is proved against a real column in BOTH lanes. A comparison, so the digest pins the 0/1 condition as well as the line.

the bar's own `t`, and the case that pins the UNIT: this platform's `t` is unix SECONDS everywhere and Pine's `time` is milliseconds, so a lane that adopted Pine's unit would be out by 1000x on every bar and every comparison a member writes against it

the ET calendar year. Flat across this corpus (all 2025), which is exactly why it is here: it is the cheapest column on which a lane resolving the zone WRONG still agrees, so it pins the plumbing while `hour` below pins the zone

the ET calendar month, 1-12. The corpus spans 2025-10-31 into 2025-11-04, so the value CHANGES inside the series -- a lane that computed the month once and filled the column would pass on any single-day fixture and fails here
the ET day of month. It rolls 31 -> 3 across the weekend gap, so a lane deriving the day by counting bars rather than reading the instant is red

⛔ THE CONVENTION CASE. `dayofweek` is PINE'S -- 1 on Sunday through 7 on Saturday -- not `Date.getDay()`'s 0-6 and not Python's 0=Monday. This corpus is Fri/Mon/Tue, so the three lanes' three natural answers are all DIFFERENT numbers here and any two of them disagreeing is a red digest rather than an off-by-one nobody notices

⛔⛔ THE DST CASE, AND THE REASON THE CLOCK IS NOT ARITHMETIC. These 579 bars cross the end of US DST (Fri 2025-10-31 EDT -> Mon 2025-11-03 EST). An implementation holding ONE UTC offset captured at import is correct on the Friday and an hour wrong on the Monday -- the `VWAP_SESSION_ANCHOR` defect exactly, in a new column. Both lanes must resolve the zone PER INSTANT from the IANA database

the ET minute, 0-59. On 5-minute bars it cycles 0,5,...,55 and NEVER repeats a value inside an hour, so a lane that memoised the minute alongside the hour (the memo is on the UTC hour) returns a constant and is red on the second bar

1 on the first bar of an ET calendar day. ⛔ THE UTC-MIDNIGHT TRAP: 20:00 ET on the EDT session IS 00:00 UTC the next day, so a lane bucketing by the UTC day opens a session on the LAST bar of a session that has not ended -- the measured $14.45 open-gap defect `VWAP_SESSION_ANCHOR` retired. Three ET days here means exactly three 1s

the bar's position in the series, 0 on the oldest. The one clock column that reads no timestamp at all, so it is also the control: it must still be right on a series whose `t` the unit gate refuses, and a lane that folded it into the gate would answer all-null

1 when the timeframe is intraday, carried with `opts: {tf: '5'}` -- the FIRST corpus case to use `interpret`'s tableVersion-2 sixth argument at all. Without the opts thread both lanes answer all-null and agree perfectly about nothing, which is why `case_opts` is a single reader for both

1 when the timeframe is daily, measured with `opts: {tf: 'D'}` on a five-minute series. ⭐ THE TIMEFRAME IS THE CALLER'S CLAIM, NOT AN INFERENCE FROM THE BARS: these bars are 5 minutes apart and this case must still answer 1, because a lane that 'helpfully' derived the timeframe from the bar spacing would silently overrule the definition's own chart

1 when the timeframe is weekly. Paired with `isdaily` above so the two 0/1 answers cross: with `tf: 'W'` this is 1 and `isdaily` is 0, and a lane that mapped every non-intraday code to one flag passes one case and fails the other

1 when the timeframe is monthly, and the LAST of the eight codes this platform ships. The four booleans are a partition over a known code: exactly one is 1 for any code in the vocabulary, and NONE is 1 for a code outside it -- `tests/fixtures/ast/clock_parity.json`'s `tf_booleans` block carries that half

⛔⛔ THE ONE ACCUMULATOR, MEASURED ACROSS THE LANES. `vwap()` binds `indicators.js::computeVWAP` and `indicator_compute.compute_vwap_raw` -- the session VWAP the chart draws and the one the alert engine fires on -- so this digest is what stops a formula's VWAP and the product's VWAP from ever becoming two numbers. ⭐ IT IS ALSO THE UTC-MIDNIGHT REGRESSION FIXTURE: these 579 bars carry the Friday 20:00 ET print that IS 00:00 UTC the next day, and the retired UTC-day bucketing wiped the accumulator there -- a measured $14.45 at the following open. A revert to it moves this digest in BOTH lanes. ⭐ AND IT IS THE FIRST ZERO-ARGUMENT CASE IN THIS CORPUS, which is the whole reason the entry is declarable at all: with no argument columns to pack there is no fabricated bar-index `t`, so the binding reads the real instant

the same accumulator restarted at an INSTANT -- 2025-11-03 12:00 ET, the middle of this corpus's second ET session -- which is the only anchor a closed-table formula can spell, because the table has exactly two argument kinds and no string literal. ⛔ THE COLUMN IS BLANK BEFORE THE ANCHOR AND EXACT AFTER IT, never a partial accumulation of the bars that came first, so a lane that started its total at bar 0 disagrees on every bar of the first session rather than on none. ⚠️ The anchor is INSIDE the series on purpose: an anchor before the first bar is NOT COMPUTABLE by declaration, because 'the first bar at or after it' would be whichever bar the caller happened to fetch

⛔ THE REQUEST-DEPENDENCE REFUSAL, MEASURED ACROSS THE LANES. The anchor is ONE SECOND before the corpus's first bar, so 'the first bar at or after it' would be whichever bar the caller happened to fetch first -- and the value at every bar would then move when the window moved, which is `lesson_a_derived_value_must_not_depend_on_the_request` and the exact defect `_functions_recurrence` says `accum`'s re-seeded window exists to prevent. Both lanes must answer NOT COMPUTABLE rather than a plausible column, and a lane that dropped the refusal produces finite rows -- which this case's `allNaN` flag turns into a named failure rather than a moved digest nobody can attribute. ⭐ IT IS THE ONLY ONE OF `avwap`'S TWO DECLARED-WINDOW REFUSALS A 579-BAR CORPUS CAN REACH: the other -- a bar more than `sessionMaxBars` past the anchor -- needs a series longer than a session, so it is railed per-lane in `tests/test_ast_vwap_parity.py` and `interpret.test.js` instead, twice on purpose.

⭐ THE BOUNDED COUNTER, AND THE ROW THAT PINS ITS SENTINEL ACROSS THE LANES. Two numbers live in one column here and they are not the same kind of fact: a COUNT (`0`..`9`) says which bar was true, and the SENTINEL `10` says none of the last ten was. A lane that let the count run past its window would still produce a plausible column -- larger numbers, no NaN, nothing red -- so the digest is what holds the cap. ⛔ AND THE LEFT EDGE IS HALF OF IT: the first bars of the series are NOT COMPUTABLE unless a true bar is actually visible in them, because `10` there would be a claim about bars nobody fetched.

⭐ THE CARRIED VALUE, AND THE ONLY ROW IN THIS CORPUS WHOSE HOLES ARE INTERIOR RATHER THAN A WARM-UP PREFIX. `valuewhen` blanks again whenever ten bars pass with no true one, so the column alternates between answered and not-computable down the middle of the series -- a lane that held the last value past its window would produce a fully finite column, which is exactly the confident-wrong-number shape the declaration exists to forbid. 🔴 ITS NaN IS LAUNDERED ON THE SCAN LANE (X23): under a comparison the holes read as a confident FALSE. Declared at `closedTable.json::_functions_bounded_state`.

⛔⛔ THE ROW THAT SPENDS THE CORPUS'S TIES. Measured on these very bars: 56 of the 5-bar `high` windows hold their maximum TWICE, and on every one of them 'the most recent bar wins' and 'the oldest bar wins' name a DIFFERENT bar -- so this digest moves if the tie-break declared in `closedTable.json::_functions_arg_extreme` is flipped in either lane. ⭐ THAT IS WHY THE WINDOW IS 5 AND NOT 20: the ruling is only pinned here for the window this case uses, and a smaller one spends more of the series' ties per bar. The CONSTRUCTED tie in `tests/test_ast_bounded_state.py` covers what a real series cannot -- a TOTAL tie, and the declared number asserted per lane rather than the two lanes agreeing with each other.

⭐ THE MIRROR, AND IT IS NOT A DUPLICATE. `low` ties 36 times over these bars where `high` ties 56, and the two entries pass OPPOSITE comparisons into the same helper -- a lane that inverted one of them would answer a perfectly plausible column of offsets and only this row would move.

⭐ THE THIRD `reads: "bars"` ENTRY, AND THE ONE THAT RETIRES AN EXCLUSION. `_functions_excluded.obv` refuses the unbounded LEVEL because it is a fact about where the fetch started; this is that level's CHANGE across a declared window, and the seed cancels. ⛔ IT IS BOUND TO THE SHIPPED ACCUMULATOR (`computeOBV` / `compute_obv_raw`, differenced 20 bars apart) rather than to a private second sum, so this digest is also the rail on those two staying one number. ⚠️ VOLUME IS THE ONLY BAR FIELD IN THIS CORPUS WITH NO TIE ANYWHERE, and it is also the field with the largest magnitudes, so this row is where a float-associativity difference between the lanes would show first.

_pine_parity: ⭐ SIX CASES, ONE PER NAME, AND EVERY ONE OF THE SIX WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN WISHED FOR: a study of 21 real published Pine scripts found `rma`, `wma`, `round`, `sign`, `na` and `nz` to be the ENTIRE manifest half of what still refused. ⚠️ THREE OF THEM EXIST BECAUSE THE TWO LANGUAGES DISAGREE BY DEFAULT and one because they disagree about a signed zero -- `round`, `sign`, and the NaN behaviour of `na`/`nz` are each a place where inheriting the host language would have produced two engines that each looked internally consistent. ⛔ `na` AND `nz` ARE THE ONLY ENTRIES IN THIS TABLE THAT DO NOT PROPAGATE NaN, so their two cases are the only ones here whose values are defined on bars the rest of the corpus reports as not computable.
_recurrence: ⭐ FIVE CASES PIN THE RECURRENCE, AND EACH PINS A DIFFERENT HALF OF IT. The bounded counter pins that the window RE-SEEDS -- a single forward pass reads 1,2,3... where the shipped one reads 12 -- the running maximum pins the scalar/column equality by being `highest(close, 20)` under another name, the sticky flag pins the ternary spine, the windowed case pins the pure/impure PARTITION and the composed lookback, and the offset case pins the line between shifting a finished column (legal) and reading the binding through a bar offset (refused). ⛔ THE BINDING IS SPELLED `self` HERE BECAUSE A CORPUS CASE IS DATA A HUMAN READS; every WALKER reads that name from `functions.accum.recurrence.binds` instead, which is why renaming it would move these five digests and nothing else.
_indicators: ⭐ THE INDICATOR ROWS (Phase F). One case per newly declared function, because `assert_corpus_covers_the_table` derives its floor FROM THE MANIFEST and a function with no case is a function whose two lanes may already disagree with every gate green. Two rows are not a function at all -- `macd_signal_by_composition` and `stoch_d_by_composition` are the COMPOSITIONS `_functions_excluded` offers in place of the two entries it refuses, so a refusal that quietly stopped being survivable moves a digest. ⛔ THE SEVENTEEN EXISTING DIGESTS DO NOT MOVE, and that is a measurement rather than a hope: not one row here edits an existing tree, and the re-record was diffed against the previous log key by key.
_allNaN: A case that is NOT COMPUTABLE ON EVERY BAR, deliberately. The domain refusals (sqrt of a negative, log of zero, an overflow, a zero divisor) are the cases where the two languages natively disagree, so they are exactly the cases worth having -- and their correct column IS all-NaN. ⛔ The flag is per-case and opt-in so the rail keeps its teeth: an UNEXPECTED all-NaN column still fails, which is what it was written to catch.
_bar_readers: ⭐⭐ THE BAR-READING ROWS. ⛔ NO COUNT IS WRITTEN HERE, AND THAT IS A CORRECTION: this note opened "THE TWO BAR-READING ROWS" and `obvN(20)` made it three on 2026-08-26 — the identical claim was corrected in `closedTable.json::_functions_bar_readers` in the SAME commit and this copy was missed, which is the whole hazard of a count mirrored across artifacts. `ast_table.bar_readers` answers it; read that. Every other case in this file is measured over columns; these two are measured over the BARS, `t` included, because their entries declare `reads: "bars"` -- and that declaration is the whole reason `vwap` stopped being refused (`closedTable.json::_functions_bar_readers`). ⛔ THEY ARE THE ONLY CASES HERE WHOSE ANSWER DEPENDS ON A TIMEZONE DATABASE RATHER THAN ON ARITHMETIC, which is what makes the cross-lane digest worth having: `Intl.DateTimeFormat` against `zoneinfo`, over a corpus that crosses a DST fallback, a weekend and the Friday 20:00 ET bar that is 00:00 UTC the next day. ⚠️ NEITHER CARRIES `opts`: a session is decided by the CALENDAR, so unlike the four timeframe booleans these answer the same column whatever timeframe the caller claims.
_bounded_state: ⭐ FIVE ROWS, ONE PER BOUNDED-STATE ENTRY, because `assert_corpus_covers_the_table` derives its floor FROM THE MANIFEST and an entry with no case is an entry whose two lanes may already disagree with every gate green. ⛔⛔ TWO OF THEM CARRY A RULING NO OTHER ROW HERE DOES: `highestbars`/`lowestbars` return an OFFSET, so when two bars of the window tie they have an answer where `highest`/`lowest` do not. Measured on these bars, 56 `high` windows and 36 `low` windows tie at 5, and every one of them separates the two conventions -- so these digests are a real rail on `closedTable.json::_functions_arg_extreme` rather than a formality. ⚠️ AND THEY ARE NOT THE WHOLE RAIL: a corpus can only pin the window a case happens to use, and it cannot contain a TOTAL tie at all. `tests/test_ast_bounded_state.py` carries the constructed one.
_clock: ⭐ THE CLOCK ROWS (tableVersion 2). One case per declared clock name, because `assert_corpus_covers_the_table` derives its floor FROM THE MANIFEST and a clock entry with no case is a name whose two lanes may already disagree with every gate green. ⛔ THESE ARE THE ONLY CASES IN THIS FILE WHOSE ANSWER DOES NOT COME FROM A PRICE -- they come from a CALENDAR, which is a second implementation on each side (`Intl.DateTimeFormat` against `zoneinfo`) rather than one formula written twice. The four `opts`-bearing rows are also the first cases in this corpus to exercise `interpret`'s trailing `opts` argument at all; a clock boolean measured WITHOUT it is two lanes agreeing on an all-null column, which is a pass about nothing.
